title: AAW installation manifest
description: The source of truth for what Advanced AI Workflows has installed into a project, where, and at what version. Written by setup-with-claude; read by --refresh, by the audit, and by any tool that needs to know whether a component is present. It exists because path probing lies in both directions: a stale .advanced-plans/ directory is not an installation, and a component installed under a global profile is invisible to a project-local probe. Every path here is absolute and free of ~ and of environment-variable references, because on some machines HOME and USERPROFILE disagree and a manifest that records ~ records nothing.

schema_version.description: Integer, incremented only on a breaking change to this schema. A reader that does not recognise the value must refuse to interpret the file rather than guess.

generated_at.description: UTC ISO 8601 instant, seconds precision, trailing Z. Local times are not accepted: two manifests written on either side of a DST boundary must remain comparable. The pattern below fixes the shape only - 2026-99-99T99:99:99Z matches it and is not a date. JSON Schema cannot express the calendar check here (format is an annotation a validator need not enforce), so readers do it: tools/aaw-audit.py before writing, tests/packaging/validate-manifest.py when validating.

generated_by.description: Name and version of whatever wrote the file, so a bad manifest can be traced to the writer that produced it.

platform.description: The operating-system family whose path conventions the absolute paths in this file follow.

project_root.description: Absolute path to the project this manifest describes. The manifest itself lives at <project_root>/.aaw/installed.json.

components.description: One entry per component the stack knows about, keyed by its canonical name. A component that has never been considered is absent; a component that was considered and is not present is recorded with installed: false, which is information a missing key cannot carry.

absolutePath.description: An absolute path in native form for the manifest's platform: a Windows drive-letter path such as C:\Users\name\project, or a POSIX path beginning with /. A tilde, a $VAR, or a %VAR% is rejected outright — those are the ambiguity this manifest exists to remove.

installed.description: Whether the component is present. This is the answer, not a hint: it is written after a sentinel file was confirmed to exist, never inferred from a data directory.

scope.description: Where the component lives. 'global' is the user profile, 'project' is this project's tree, 'none' is used when the component is not installed and therefore has no location.

install_path.description: Absolute path to the installed component's root directory.

sentinel.description: Absolute path to the single file whose existence was checked. Recording it makes the claim falsifiable: a reader can check the same path and disagree.

version.description: The component's version as reported by its own VERSION file or manifest, or the literal 'unknown' when it does not publish one. 'unknown' is a real answer and is preferred to omitting the field or inventing a number.

deprecated.description: ISO date on which this component was deprecated by the programme. Present only for deprecated components, which are recorded rather than deleted so that a pre-existing install is not silently re-detected as wanted.

allOf.description: An installed component must say where it is, what proved it, and what version it is. Without those three the entry is an assertion rather than a record.
A component that is not installed has no location, and must not carry a stale one from a previous run.
Conversely, scope 'none' is reserved for components that are not installed.
